queue.notes: Part 2 of grow. Facts checked: house cat ~25 cm at shoulder (x10 = elephant), dust mite 0.25-0.3 mm, corneocyte (skin flake) ~30-40 um, E. coli ~2 um, visible light 380-700 nm, DNA helix ~2 nm wide, atoms ~0.1-0.5 nm. Hero 'Chris' voice clips not used: audio/voices/hero_chris/ is not in the repo (gitignored) and the single library mp3 in fetched/ is unlabeled, so lines could not be identified without listening; speech bubbles carry the hero's reactions instead.

style_notes: Counter variety: big pill (ours), elegant serif top-left with small sub-label (electrons/earth-spin/run-speed refs), progress bar for time-lapses (1000-years ref).
Add a tier badge under the counter that upgrades each beat (e.g. HUMAN → BUILDING → MOUNTAIN → PLANET), like the run-speed ref's rank tags.
Expressive character faces and reactions at each beat (Roblox school-story ref); one recurring side character per episode (neighbor, granny, mom, rival).
One-sentence caption per beat in italic serif OR word-by-word pop captions; never both at the same spot.
Endings loop or restart (run-speed ref restarts at 'Minute 0'), or tease the part 2 that is already in the plan.
Do not copy other creators' premises, characters or captions; take the format, not the content.

styles.A_explainer: Current style. Female narrator (Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.1), 2nd person 'you', big title + pill counter, word-by-word captions, 40–48 s.
styles.B_silent_cinematic: NO voiceover (like the electrons / Earth-stops-spinning / run-speed references). Music + sound design carry it. One short italic serif line per beat (e.g. 'You do not. Nothing does.'), elegant small serif counter top-left with a sub-label and an upgrading tier badge, slower camera, colour-graded cinematic look. 35–45 s.
styles.C_first_person_story: A character tells it as 'I…' (like the golden-drops / Roblox school-story references): opens mid-drama ('I looked in the mirror this morning, and…'), states the world's rule, personal stakes, a twist, cliffhanger. Fast and emotional (~3.5–4 words/s), expressive blocky character with big eyes/mouth reacting every beat, word-by-word captions. Male voice (Kokoro am_puck or am_michael). 61–75 s so TikTok counts it as > 1 min.
styles.D_warm_explainer: Calm, comforting 'you' narrator with a small joke in every beat (like the 'everyone slept 1,000 years' reference: 'At least the rent has finally gone down', 'Earth is slowly cleaning out its attic'). Timeline/progress-bar counter, cozy lighting, a cute side character (raccoon/parrot style). Male voice (Kokoro bm_george or am_michael), ~2.6 words/s, 61–75 s.

rules: Length 30–38 s total (Instagram data: viewers left at ~20 s of 48 s, 42% watched, 35% skip).
Cold open: the first 0.0–1.0 s shows the MOST extreme moment of the video (the payoff image), with the counter already moving fast and the title on screen; then a whoosh cut to 'the start'.
Hook line ≤ 2 s and must start at 0.1 s. No slow intro, no static counter at 0.
A new visual change every 2–3 s; cut beats that don't escalate.
Looping ending: the last frame matches/flows into the first frame so the video replays seamlessly; no long outro, the 'follow for part 2' line ≤ 1.5 s.
End with a one-line question to drive comments (e.g. 'Which hiccup would you survive?') and repeat it in the caption.

visual_rules.approved: 2026-11-09 by owner (feedback: videos felt dry, characters dead, effects just a beam/light)
visual_rules.reference_test: sneeze v3 (engine/scenes/sneeze3.js) is the template to copy patterns from
rules: Characters must feel alive: use lib.js setFace() every frame (brows, eye size, mouth shape, pupil look direction) with a different expression for each beat, then life() for breathing, blinking, glances and idle sway. Characters react to every event (shock, cringe, look at the damage).

Add at least one other character who reacts: a neighbor, a pet, a family member. Use 3–6 short speech bubbles (drawBubble, 1–3 words, funny) anchored to heads, as in the reference videos ('Still good.', 'MY HAT!').

Big events are EXPANDING WAVES, never a beam or a single flash: makeShockwave() (dust wall ring, glowing shell, ground ring) plus a reaction in the world as the front passes (suburb.wave(): roofs rip off and tumble, trees flatten, cars slide). Each topic gets its own fitting spreading effect (a heat wave that browns lawns outward, a frost front, a crack network, a flood front, etc.).
Aerial/city shots use makeSuburb(): a block grid with streets both ways, gable roofs, lawns, driveways, trees, cars and pools. No plain boxes on a flat green plane.

Numbers sit on the left side as a small counter (drawSideCounter: small label, big number, italic comparison note like 'faster than sound'), placed under the title, as in the reference videos. Never a big box in the middle of the screen. Keep the right edge clear (platform buttons).

Sound: always a background song (music2.song: drums, bass, arp, lead that build with the intensity curve) plus environment beds (music2.amb: city/wind/space/fire) under the voice and SFX. Music must sit clearly under the voice (music_gain ≈ 0.38, amb gain ≈ 0.25–0.3).
Also export a no-music version for TikTok (music_gain 0), so the owner can add a trending sound in the app (copyrighted songs are never baked into the file).
Busy, living world (owner, Nov 9): pedestrians walking on the sidewalks, cars actually driving on the streets (not only parked), more bystanders who all react (stop, point, run, film with phones).
Anything flying through the sky shares it with planes/helicopters/birds that pass close by (the flying person passes a plane, a passenger at the window reacts).

Breakage must read instantly: when something punches through a wall/door, the hole is a crisp cartoon cut-out of its exact silhouette (star pose, arms and legs out), shown in a 0.5 s slow-motion beat from the far side with light shining through the hole and dust puffing out of the outline, then debris bursts outward. Never a random scatter of blocks.
Pacing (owner, Nov 9 — middle point between our 4 s and the reference's 1.4 s): a new shot or a big camera move every ~2–2.5 s.
Use a continuous follow-camera when it helps (e.g. follow the character while he flies instead of cutting away).

2–4 object close-ups/inserts per video (the cat mid-air, the hat, the mailbox, a glass shard, a bystander's phone screen filming it). Keep inventing small interactive touches like these — the owner wants more of them.
The counter changes meaning per chapter (e.g. SNEEZE SPEED → DISTANCE FLOWN → TIME TO LANDING) and always moves: ticking decimals, colour shifts to orange/red as danger rises.

Every milestone gets a real-world comparison SHOWN on screen, side by side, with a small label (a jet next to the sneeze wind, a bullet racing it, a rocket at escape velocity, a satellite) so viewers instantly get what the number means.
Name tags only for a character's first appearance (intro), optional.
Recurring cast links the episodes (shared universe): MITTENS the cat appears regularly (give her a proper intro the first time — people love animals), plus Dave the neighbour and the main character.
Special cartoon faces at peak moments: heart eyes, star eyes, tears, sweat drop, dizzy swirl.
Occasionally (not every video) a fake live-chat/phone-comment overlay or a background bystander shouting a funny line.
Floating particles (embers, dust motes, sparkles) present but subtle — not too much, not too little.
Ending: return to the opening scene but changed (loop + twist), then the question, then a 'Part 2' tease.

Title (owner loved the 'boyfriend' reference, Nov 9): flash cold open (0.5 s of the craziest moment + one punch word like 'SNIP.'), then the title types in word by word over a wide establishing shot, holds ~3 s and then animates OUT (by ~5 s). After that only the side counter stays at the top. Optional time-jump card ('⏮ 3 minutes earlier').
Counter sub-label shows place + time and updates with the story ('YOUR APARTMENT · 9:41 PM' → 'DOWNTOWN · 9:43 PM' → 'EARTH ORBIT').

Talking characters: short punchy speech bubbles in quick back-and-forth (white rounded bubble, 2–6 words), mouths moving while they talk, extreme close-up faces for big reactions (huge eyes, wide open mouth), countdown numbers (3, 2, 1) popping next to the bubbles when tension builds.
Crowds: when the story scales up, show LOTS of people (hundreds to thousands, instanced) filling streets, plus people in the background of normal shots.
Buildings with detail: lit windows, varied facades and heights, dusk/evening light when it fits — never plain boxes.

Switch perspective when it matters: first-person (hands on the steering wheel, hands holding the object) for the start or key moments, then third-person behind/side views, and back to first-person for the ending (owner approved Nov 9). Body/'what if YOU' premises: short POV start; calm world/history premises can stay mostly POV; comedy/action stays mostly third-person.
Shareable ending line when it fits the topic (e.g. 'Send this to your boyfriend.') instead of only 'follow'.

Character voices (owner, Nov 9): the main character uses the ElevenLabs 'Chris' voice clip library in engine/audio/voices/hero_chris/ (sneezes, hic, whoa, oh no, uh-oh, wait what, nope, ow, seriously, Mittens, help, excuse me, sorry, laugh, phew, wow, huh, aaah) — NOT Kokoro male voices (owner: robotic). Lines go ONLY in gaps between narrator lines, 3–4 per video. New lines: vidIQ vidiq_voiceover_generate (voiceId iP95p4xoKVk53GoZ742B, 28 credits per ≤1000 chars — batch many lines in ONE call, only when the library lacks a needed line; vidIQ has ~150 credits/month), then add 'name url' to fetch/<file>.txt and push: the fetch-media GitHub workflow downloads it into fetched/ (assets.vidiq.com is blocked from the sandbox). Side characters may keep Kokoro (granny bf_emma) until we record better ones.

format_v4.approved: 2026-11-10 by owner. SUPERSEDES hook_rules/visual_rules wherever they conflict.
format_v4.why: Own data: viewers give ~22 s (YouTube 23 s avg, Instagram 22 s) on 47 s videos. Reference account @man_ia_c (297K followers, 5M likes, 24 videos): its hits are all 'What if <basic thing> disappeared for 5 seconds?' (19M, 14.1M, 6M, 5.2M, 4.2M) with one fixed look.
rules: PREMISE: happens to the WHOLE WORLD (not one person), with a short time limit: 'What if <something basic> <vanished/doubled/stopped> for 5 seconds?'. History premises ('what if the asteroid missed') are also fine.

COUNTER = COUNTDOWN: open on a calm, detailed everyday scene with '<THING> DISAPPEARS IN 0:05.000' ticking down in milliseconds on the left; at zero the event happens; then a second counter runs '0:01 … 0:05' through the consequences, one clear consequence per second, each bigger in scale (street → city → planet). Then 'it comes back' and the aftermath.
HOOK (owner): 2.5–3 s, shown clearly and slightly slowed — the most extreme consequence — with one teaser narrator line, then a '<< N SECONDS EARLIER' card, then the calm start. Never a 0.5 s flash.
LENGTH: 25–30 s for YouTube/Instagram/TikTok. (A 61–70 s TikTok cut only once the account nears 10K followers and the owner confirms the rewards programme is open to him.)

ONE LOCKED LOOK for at least 10 videos: same title style and position, same countdown style, same calm-opening structure, same music family, city = engine/scenes/nyc.js style (street grid, towers with windows, taxis, crowds, park, rivers). Do not restyle between videos.
LESS TEXT: title, countdown, word-by-word captions. At most 2 speech bubbles and 1 punch caption per video. No step-by-step 'stage 1…7' escalation.

KEEP from before: detailed city, crowds, expanding waves, background song + ambience, loop ending (last shot flows into the hook), Mittens as a small recurring background detail (never the focus), narrator af_heart, hero voice clips only in gaps.
SUBSCRIBE: no 'follow for part 2' line. (Owner is choosing between: viewers pick tomorrow's what-if in comments / crediting the winner / Mittens survival counter — do not add until he picks.)
